title: Network node immunization: improving Netshield algorithm through random rooted forests
summary: We are interested in the so-called multiple-node immunization problem for complex networks under attack by a viral agent. It consists in identifying and removing a set of nodes of size $k$ in a graph to maximize the impeding of virus spread. A few approaches have been proposed in the literature based on numerical and theoretical insights on how classical models for virus spread evolve on graphs.
